what: Elastic makes Elasticsearch, the open-source search engine companies use to search their own data, and sells the hosted and enterprise versions used for log analysis, security monitoring and site search.
customers: Software engineering, security and operations teams at companies of every size.
money: the hosted service on Amazon, Google and Microsoft clouds
software run on customers' own infrastructure
moat: Open-source adoption that puts Elasticsearch inside thousands of companies before anyone pays, with the paid tiers selling to teams already dependent on it.
risks: Amazon's OpenSearch fork competes with a free alternative
Growth has slowed as customers optimise how much data they store
19 times earnings looks cheap but reported profit includes a large one-off tax benefit
opportunities: A 21.1% net margin and $322M of free cash flow on $1.9B of revenue
Revenue grew from $862M to $1.7B in four years with cloud growing fastest
Analysts see about 39% upside, with 26 covering the stock, and vector search for AI applications is a new use
watch: Elastic Cloud revenue growth and net expansion rate.
